finding_resolutions.basis: Tuple reservations now cover disabled and retired history. Disablement is terminal in the first profile, and replacement requires a distinct qualified client ID and installation identity. Fresh authentication of unchanged old token bytes after replacement/restart remains bound to the retired original and denied. This closes the temporal remapping ambiguity.

The execution host owns time assurance. SystemTime, JWT verification and a persisted timestamp are explicitly insufficient to establish elapsed downtime. Restart begins held pending an accepted current time bound. The proposed test covers actual downtime expiry followed by a plausible earlier clock, and fixture evidence is distinguished from production assurance.

A2.1 now explicitly owns guarded response emission, both response/invalidation serial orderings and the actual response-write gate. Its allocation and first executable checkpoint include that composition, persistence consumption and the clock/restart assurance choice.
